html:
The Malgana, shown on the map as Malkana from 1600 to 1815, are an Aboriginal Australian people of Shark Bay on the west coast of Western Australia. Their neighbours were the Yinggarda to the north and the Nhanda to the south.

Their coast saw some of the first Europeans to reach Australia. In 1616 the Dutch captain Dirk Hartog, sailing for the Dutch East India Company, landed on the island now named after him and left an inscribed pewter plate. William Dampier visited in 1699 and named Shark Bay. Pearling and sheep stations came in the late 1800s. Shark Bay, with its stromatolites and seagrass meadows, became a World Heritage site in 1991.
